title: Radius from arc length and angle
source: Theory P1-4.2 Quick check 2 / Worked example 4.3 (12 = r x 1.5, r=8); book p.105
stem: A sector has an angle of \(\dfrac{{k|int}}{2}\) radians and an arc length of \({s|int}\,\mathrm{cm}\). Find the radius of the sector.

steps.name: M
steps.note: Use s=r theta with theta in radians.

contexts.note: angle written as k/2 so 1.5 appears as 3/2

contexts.stem: An arc of length \({s|int}\,\mathrm{cm}\) subtends an angle of \(\dfrac{{k|int}}{2}\) radians at the centre. Find the radius of the circle.
A sector of a circle has arc length \({s|int}\,\mathrm{cm}\) and angle \(\dfrac{{k|int}}{2}\) radians. Find the radius.

title: Numerical arc length, 3 significant figures
source: Theory P1-4.2 Quick check 3 (arc of radius 8 cm and angle 2.4 rad is 19.2 cm); book Exercise 4B style, pp.105–106
stem: Find the length of an arc of radius \({r|int}\,\mathrm{cm}\) that subtends an angle of \({th|raw}\) radians at the centre, correct to 3 significant figures.

steps.name: L
steps.note: Correct to 3 significant figures, including significant trailing zeros.

contexts.note: theta given as a one-decimal-place radian measure t/10; t=10 (1 radian) excluded only to avoid a trivial r x 1

title: Metal plate formed by removing a segment

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2012). Official MS for (i): cosine rule or 2 r sin(theta/2), 14.9 cm (A1). For (ii): M1 uses s=r theta with 2.4 or with pi-2.4? MS: Perimeter=(i)+r theta, theta=2 pi-2.4 (B1), 46.0 cm (A1). Part (iii) (area) is P1-4.3 content and is omitted. A source-faithful static redraw is embedded; no figure field or renderer was added. Expressions are numeric literals equal to 16 sin(1.2) and that plus 8(2 pi-2.4), because the practice engine's math object has no sin.

stem: The diagram shows a metal plate made by removing a segment from a circle with centre \(O\) and radius \(8\,\mathrm{cm}\). The line \(AB\) is a chord of the circle and angle \(AOB=2.4\) radians. Find (i) the length of \(AB\), (ii) the perimeter of the plate.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: Length of the chord: \(AB=2\times 8\times\sin(1.2)\) (or the cosine rule in triangle \(AOB\)).
steps.note: MS: cosine rule or 2 r sin(1/2 * 2.4); any complete valid method.

parts.stem: Find the perimeter of the plate.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: The remaining perimeter is the chord plus the major arc: \((i)+r\theta\) with \(\theta=2\pi-2.4\).
steps.note: MS: M1 uses s=r theta with 2.4, or pi-2.4.

steps.name: P
steps.note: MS: 46.0 cm. (Anywhere in parts (ii) or (iii). Adds 31.1 to (i).)
